scope: A separate geometry-only client records request-to-callback-handler and callback-to-next-attempt client wall times, successful draw stages and separate compositor presentation feedback. This is bounded diagnostic and restoration evidence, not compositor-only bottleneck attribution or performance acceptance.

sources.scope: The archived diagnostic, currently recorded managed performance trial and accepted main are separate identities. No new managed desktop deployment or performance acceptance is implied.
sources.native_execution_identity_scope: Actual native execution used archived91b. A later clean-main integration of the same instrumentation is a different source identity; this receipt is not native execution or release validation of that later branch.

local_validation.scope: Archived runtime and diagnostic example checks; not a full workspace gate or final documentation-head CI result.

post_run_normal_state.scope: Ordinary pause/resume saves are allowed to replace the settings inode and timestamps by the preexisting reviewed policy. Diagnostic socket/lock activity may change runtime-parent entry size/timestamps. An initial overstrict metadata comparison was retained as false; the existing policy, not a new weakened rule, passed. Fresh facts independently match the actual native final state.

closed_event_window.scope: Only closed event IDs after the first snapshot watermark through the final snapshot. Per-poll ring trimming is normal; contiguous merged IDs and counter deltas establish that retained closed events were not lost.

correlation.scope: The final outstanding callback request is normal endpoint state, not an unmatched observed callback. No artificial request or cross-generation join was made.

client_timings_ms.scope: All use one diagnostic process Instant epoch. Request time is sampled immediately before wl_surface.frame is marshalled, inside the render presentation closure, before the surrounding attempt finishes. Handler entry is recorded before SDK routing; next-attempt timing can include intentional idle in general. Request-to-handler includes remaining render/present work, protocol transport/flush, compositor decisions, OS scheduling and client event dispatch; it does not isolate any one of them.

raw_core_callback_data.scope: Core callback_data_ms has an undefined clock base and stays separate from local Instant and wp_presentation. No absolute cross-clock subtraction or wall-clock inference.

presentation.scope: Distinct successful presentation-feedback intervals in the compositor-provided clock. This is not measured pixel change, scanout FPS or a performance-target acceptance.

successful_submission_cpu_profiles.scope: Successful submission CPU wall time including driver waits; not GPU execution, application updates, event-queue delay or full-loop time. These timers have different endpoints from the attempt trace and must not be added as independent disjoint stages.

frame_window_joins.scope: Presentation and CPU/closed-event windows have different endpoint filters. The two terminal rows lie beyond the selected feedback window and are not counted as dropped/error frames.

recipe.quantiles: Nearest rank: sort N values and take ceil(N*p)-1 for p50/p95/p99; arithmetic means.
recipe.cadence: Adjacent interval count divided by last minus first timestamp in that same clock.
recipe.event_contiguity: Selected event IDs equal the exact first.events_total+1 through last.events_total; callback and completed-attempt counts equal counter deltas.

static_visual_review.observation: Opaque blue diagnostic background and cyan rounded rectangle are visible, partly obscured by existing shell widgets.
static_visual_review.scope: A separate human static image review; raw flags remain unchanged. No screenshot or private capture path is published.

observations: In this capture, most measured request-to-next-attempt time elapsed before callback-handler entry; handler entry to the next admitted attempt was short. This bounds a client-visible interval and does not identify compositor, transport, OS or event-dispatch cause.

Earlier video, shape-only and shape-CPU observations remain separate source/workload/profile captures. The lower cadence here cannot be attributed to tracing, host load or a product regression without a matched eligible comparison.
limits: One virtual output and one partial static visual review; no physical-output, multi-output, animation smoothness or full-surface fidelity acceptance.
No host-pressure eligibility collector or matched before/after comparison; no performance target acceptance.
No queue-source wrapping or dispatch-cycle timing was added; request-to-handler combines several systems.
privacy: Only sanitized aggregate measurements and source/evidence hashes are published; no native object IDs, process IDs, settings hashes, source media, private paths or raw captures.
